    writer.writeSessionCookie(id, response.proxy());\n\n        eq(\"exactly one Set-Cookie emitted\", 1, response.cookies.size());\n        Cookie cookie = response.cookies.get(0);\n        eq(\"cookie name\", \"__Host-PORTAL_SESSION\", cookie.getName());\n        eq(\"cookie value is the identifier\", GOOD, cookie.getValue());\n        eq(\"cookie path\", \"/\", cookie.getPath());\n        ok(\"cookie is HttpOnly\", cookie.isHttpOnly());\n        ok(\"cookie is Secure\", cookie.getSecure());\n        eq(\"cookie carries no expiry attribute\", -1, cookie.getMaxAge());\n        ok(\"cookie has no Domain attribute\", cookie.getDomain() == null);\n        eq(\"SameSite rendered by the component\", \"Strict\", cookie.getAttribute(\"SameSite\"));\n        eq(\"Cache-Control set to no-store\", \"no-store, max-age=0\",\n                response.header(\"Cache-Control\"));\n        eq(\"Pragma set to no-cache\", \"no-cache\", response.header(\"Pragma\"));\n        ok(\"no cookie attribute is settable by the caller\",\n                response.cookies.size() == 1 && cookie.getValue().equals(GOOD));\n\n        Recording nullResponse = Recording.create();\n        try {\n            writer.writeSessionCookie(null, nullResponse.proxy());\n            ok(\"null identifier refused\", false);\n        } catch (InvalidSessionIdentifierException expected) {\n            eq(\"null identifier refused\", SessionId.Rejection.ABSENT, expected.rejection());\n        }\n        ok(\"no cookie written for a null identifier\", nullResponse.cookies.isEmpty());\n\n        // Second gate: build a SessionId whose payload is junk, bypassing the public factory, to\n        // prove the writer does not rely on the caller having validated.\n        Constructor<SessionId> tailgate = SessionId.class.getDeclaredConstructor(String.class);\n        tailgate.setAccessible(true);\n        String[] junk = {repeat('a', 43), \"short\", GOOD + \"; Domain=evil\", repeat('a', 200),\n                GOOD.substring(0, 42) + \" \"};\n        for (String candidate : junk) {\n            SessionId smuggled = tailgate.newInstance(candidate);\n            Recording guarded = Recording.create();\n            try {\n                writer.writeSessionCookie(smuggled, guarded.proxy());\n                ok(\"writer blocks a smuggled value \" + describe(candidate), false);\n            } catch (InvalidSessionIdentifierException blocked) {\n                ok(\"writer blocks a smuggled value \" + describe(candidate) + \" (\"\n                        + blocked.rejection() + ')', true);\n            }\n            ok(\"no cookie written for the smuggled value\", guarded.cookies.isEmpty());\n        }\n        throwsIae(\"writer refuses a null response\", () -> {\n            try {\n                writer.writeSessionCookie(id, null);\n            } catch (InvalidSessionIdentifierException impossible) {\n                throw new IllegalStateException(impossible);\n            }\n        });\n        ok(\"writer exposes its policy\", writer.policy() == policy);\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ service\n\n    private static void service() throws Exception {\n        begin(\"HANDOFF DECISION: fail closed, uniform refusal, budget fairness\");\n        SessionCookiePolicy policy = SessionCookiePolicy.of(null, null, null);\n        CountingVerifier store = new CountingVerifier(GOOD);\n        AttemptLimiter generous = new AttemptLimiter(60, 100, 1000, 1000);\n        SessionHandoffService service = new SessionHandoffService(policy, store, generous);\n\n        SessionHandoffService.Decision granted = service.handle(\n                new SessionHandoffService.Request(GOOD, ClientAddress.parse(\"203.0.113.7\")));\n        eq(\"valid asserted identifier is issued\", SessionHandoffService.Outcome.ISSUED, granted.outcome());\n        eq(\"issued decision carries the identifier\", GOOD, granted.sessionIdentifier().value());\n        eq(\"store was consulted exactly once\", 1, store.calls);\n\n        SessionHandoffService noVerifier = new SessionHandoffService(policy, null,\n                new AttemptLimiter(60, 100, 1000, 1000));\n        eq(\"a missing verifier fails closed\", SessionHandoffService.Outcome.REFUSED_UNAUTHENTICATED,\n                noVerifier.handle(new SessionHandoffService.Request(GOOD,\n                        ClientAddress.parse(\"203.0.113.7\"))).outcome());\n\n        SessionHandoffService throwingStore = new SessionHandoffService(policy,\n                new SessionHandoffService.SessionStateVerifier() {\n                    @Override\n                    public boolean isSessionValid(String sessionId) {\n                        throw new IllegalStateException(\"datastore down\");\n                    }\n                }, new AttemptLimiter(60, 100, 1000, 1000));\n        eq(\"a verifier that throws is treated as 'no'\",\n                SessionHandoffService.Outcome.REFUSED_UNAUTHENTICATED,\n                throwingStore.handle(new SessionHandoffService.Request(GOOD,\n                        ClientAddress.parse(\"203.0.113.7\"))).outcome());\n\n        CountingVerifier unknownSessionStore = new CountingVerifier(\"Other-Session-Id-That-Is-Long-Enough-Xx9\");\n        SessionHandoffService unknown = new SessionHandoffService(policy, unknownSessionStore,\n                new AttemptLimiter(60, 100, 1000, 1000));\n        eq(\"a well-formed identifier the store does not know is refused\",\n                SessionHandoffService.Outcome.REFUSED_UNAUTHENTICATED,\n                unknown.handle(new SessionHandoffService.Request(GOOD,\n                        ClientAddress.parse(\"203.0.113.7\"))).outcome());\n\n        CountingVerifier untouched = new CountingVerifier(GOOD);\n        SessionHandoffService budgetService = new SessionHandoffService(policy, untouched,\n                new AttemptLimiter(60, 100, 1000, 1000));\n        for (String malformed : new String[]{null, \"\", \"short\", repeat('a', 43), GOOD + \"\\t\"}) {\n            eq(\"malformed assertion is refused before any lookup\",\n                    SessionHandoffService.Outcome.REFUSED_INVALID_ASSERTION,\n                    budgetService.handle(new SessionHandoffService.Request(malformed,\n                            ClientAddress.parse(\"203.0.113.8\"))).outcome());\n        }\n        eq(\"a malformed assertion never reaches the session store\", 0, untouched.calls);\n\n        // Flooding garbage must not spend a legitimate client's allowance.\n        AttemptLimiter oneShot = new AttemptLimiter(60, 1, 1000, 1000);\n        SessionHandoffService tight = new SessionHandoffService(policy, new CountingVerifier(GOOD), oneShot);\n        ClientAddress victim = ClientAddress.parse(\"198.51.100.9\");\n        for (int i = 0; i < 50; i++) {\n            tight.handle(new SessionHandoffService.Request(\"garbage\", victim));\n        }\n        eq(\"50 malformed requests did not consume the victim's single allowance\",\n                SessionHandoffService.Outcome.ISSUED,\n                tight.handle(new SessionHandoffService.Request(GOOD, victim)).outcome());\n\n        // Rate limiting, and the shape of the limited outcome.\n        AttemptLimiter singleUse = new AttemptLimiter(60, 1, 1000, 1000);\n        SessionHandoffService limited = new SessionHandoffService(policy, new CountingVerifier(GOOD),\n                singleUse);\n        ClientAddress floodSource = ClientAddress.parse(\"192.0.2.55\");\n        eq(\"first handoff allowed\", SessionHandoffService.Outcome.ISSUED,\n                limited.handle(new SessionHandoffService.Request(GOOD, floodSource)).outcome());\n        SessionHandoffService.Decision second =\n                limited.handle(new SessionHandoffService.Request(GOOD, floodSource));\n        eq(\"second handoff from the same source is limited\",\n                SessionHandoffService.Outcome.LIMITED_SOURCE, second.outcome());\n        ok(\"a limited refusal carries a positive Retry-After\", second.retryAfterSeconds() >= 1);\n        eq(\"a different source is unaffected by one source's limit\",\n                SessionHandoffService.Outcome.ISSUED,\n                limited.handle(new SessionHandoffService.Request(GOOD,\n                        ClientAddress.parse(\"192.0.2.56\"))).outcome());\n\n        eq(\"a null request is refused\", SessionHandoffService.Outcome.REFUSED_UNAVAILABLE,\n                service.handle(null).outcome());\n        ok(\"decision toString names the outcome only\",\n                granted.toString().equals(\"Decision[ISSUED]\") && !granted.toString().contains(GOOD));\n        ok(\"service toString carries no identifier\", !service.toString().contains(GOOD));\n        ok(\"request without a source uses the unknown bucket\",\n                service.handle(new SessionHandoffService.Request(GOOD, null)).outcome()\n                        == SessionHandoffService.Outcome.ISSUED);\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ limiter\n\n    private static void limiter() throws Exception {\n        begin(\"ATTEMPT LIMITER: atomicity, fairness, bounded state\");\n        MutableClock clock = new MutableClock(1_000L);\n        AttemptLimiter limiter = new AttemptLimiter(60, 3, 1000, 1000, clock);\n        ClientAddress source = ClientAddress.parse(\"203.0.113.1\");\n        for (int i = 1; i <= 3; i++) {\n            eq(\"attempt \" + i + \" of 3 allowed\", AttemptLimiter.Decision.ALLOWED, limiter.tryAcquire(source));\n        }\n        eq(\"attempt 4 is limited\", AttemptLimiter.Decision.LIMITED_PER_SOURCE, limiter.tryAcquire(source));\n        clock.advance(59_000L);\n        eq(\"still limited 59 s later\", AttemptLimiter.Decision.LIMITED_PER_SOURCE, limiter.tryAcquire(source));\n        clock.advance(2_000L);\n        eq(\"allowed again after the window rolls\", AttemptLimiter.Decision.ALLOWED, limiter.tryAcquire(source));\n        ok(\"a denied attempt did not consume allowance\", limiter.trackedSources() == 1);\n\n        // Global saturation must not spend the source's own allowance.\n        MutableClock globalClock = new MutableClock(0L);\n        AttemptLimiter globalTight = new AttemptLimiter(60, 10, 2, 1000, globalClock);\n        eq(\"first global slot\", AttemptLimiter.Decision.ALLOWED,\n                globalTight.tryAcquire(ClientAddress.parse(\"203.0.113.10\")));\n        eq(\"second global slot\", AttemptLimiter.Decision.ALLOWED,\n                globalTight.tryAcquire(ClientAddress.parse(\"203.0.113.11\")));\n        eq(\"third request hits the global lane\", AttemptLimiter.Decision.LIMITED_GLOBALLY,\n                globalTight.tryAcquire(ClientAddress.parse(\"203.0.113.12\")));\n        // 198.51.100.1 has never requested; it must see the global wall, not a personal one, and the\n        // decision must be the distinguishable global one so the response can be honest.\n        eq(\"a brand new source also sees the global wall, not a personal block\",\n                AttemptLimiter.Decision.LIMITED_GLOBALLY,\n                globalTight.tryAcquire(ClientAddress.parse(\"198.51.100.1\")));\n\n        // Concurrency: 16 threads hammering one bucket must not exceed the ceiling by one.\n        for (int round = 0; round < 3; round++) {\n            final AttemptLimiter race = new AttemptLimiter(600, 100, 100000, 10000);\n            final ClientAddress shared = ClientAddress.parse(\"203.0.113.99\");\n            final int threads = 16;\n            final int perThread = 40;\n            final CountDownLatch ready = new CountDownLatch(threads);\n            final CountDownLatch go = new CountDownLatch(1);\n            final AtomicInteger allowed = new AtomicInteger();\n            final AtomicInteger errors = new AtomicInteger();\n            Thread[] workers = new Thread[threads];\n            for (int t = 0; t < threads; t++) {\n                workers[t] = new Thread(new Runnable() {\n                    @Override\n                    public void run() {\n                        ready.countDown();\n                        try {\n                            go.await();\n                            for (int i = 0; i < perThread; i++) {\n                                if (race.tryAcquire(shared) == AttemptLimiter.Decision.ALLOWED) {\n                                    allowed.incrementAndGet();\n                                }\n                            }\n                        } catch (InterruptedException lost) {\n                            errors.incrementAndGet();\n                        } catch (RuntimeException broken) {\n                            errors.incrementAndGet();\n                        }\n                    }\n                });\n                workers[t].start();\n            }\n            ready.await();\n            go.countDown();\n            for (Thread worker : workers) {\n                worker.join();\n            }\n            eq(\"round \" + round + \": no worker failed\", 0, errors.get());\n            eq(\"round \" + round + \": exactly the ceiling admitted across \" + (threads * perThread)\n                    + \" racing requests\", 100, allowed.get());\n        }\n\n        // Unknown source shares one reduced lane: 4x stricter than a named source.\n        MutableClock unknownClock = new MutableClock(0L);\n        AttemptLimiter unknownLimiter = new AttemptLimiter(60, 8, 1000, 1000, unknownClock);\n        int unknownAllowed = 0;\n        for (int i = 0; i < 40; i++) {\n            if (unknownLimiter.tryAcquire(ClientAddress.UNKNOWN) == AttemptLimiter.Decision.ALLOWED) {\n                unknownAllowed++;\n            }\n        }\n        eq(\"unknown-source allowance is max(1, perSource/4)\", 2, unknownAllowed);\n\n        // Bucket growth is capped and sheds instead of exhausting memory.\n        MutableClock capClock = new MutableClock(0L);\n        AttemptLimiter capped = new AttemptLimiter(60, 1000, 100000, 5, capClock);\n        for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++) {\n            capped.tryAcquire(ClientAddress.parse(\"203.0.113.\" + (i + 1)));\n        }\n        eq(\"cap reached\", 5, capped.trackedSources());\n        eq(\"a sixth distinct source is shed, not tracked\",\n                AttemptLimiter.Decision.LIMITED_TRACKING_SATURATED,\n                capped.tryAcquire(ClientAddress.parse(\"198.51.100.77\")));\n        eq(\"tracking stayed at the cap\", 5, capped.trackedSources());\n        capClock.advance(61_000L);\n        eq(\"after the window rolls, shed buckets are evicted to admit a new source\",\n                AttemptLimiter.Decision.ALLOWED, capped.tryAcquire(ClientAddress.parse(\"198.51.100.78\")));\n\n        ok(\"Retry-After is always at least one second\", capped.retryAfterSeconds(null) >= 1\n                && capped.retryAfterSeconds(ClientAddress.parse(\"203.0.113.1\")) >= 1);\n\n        throwsIae(\"refuses a zero window rather than reading it as unlimited\",\n                () -> new AttemptLimiter(0, 10, 100, 100));\n        throwsIae(\"refuses a zero per-source ceiling\", () -> new AttemptLimiter(60, 0, 100, 100));\n        throwsIae(\"refuses a zero global ceiling\", () -> new AttemptLimiter(60, 10, 0, 100));\n        throwsIae(\"refuses a zero bucket cap\", () -> new AttemptLimiter(60, 10, 100, 0));\n        throwsIae(\"refuses an over-long window\", () -> new AttemptLimiter(999999, 10, 100, 100));\n        throwsIae(\"refuses an over-large per-source ceiling\",\n                () -> new AttemptLimiter(60, 100000, 100000, 100));\n        throwsIae(\"refuses a negative window\", () -> new AttemptLimiter(-5, 10, 100, 100));\n        ok(\"limiter toString carries no client address\",\n                !limiter.toString().contains(\"203.0.113\") && limiter.toString().contains(\"perSource=3\"));\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ client address\n\n    private static void clientAddress() {\n        begin(\"CLIENT ADDRESS canonicalisation (fair buckets, no DNS, no injection)\");\n        eq(\"::1 and its long form share a bucket\",\n                ClientAddress.parse(\"0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1\").key(), ClientAddress.parse(\"::1\").key());\n        eq(\"uppercase IPv6 shares a bucket\", ClientAddress.parse(\"2001:DB8::1\").key(),\n                ClientAddress.parse(\"2001:db8::1\").key());\n        eq(\"an IPv4-mapped address joins its IPv4 bucket\",\n                ClientAddress.parse(\"127.0.0.1\").key(),       .equals(ClientAddress.parse(\"2001:db8:0:2::11\").key()));\n        eq(\"a plain IPv4 address is canonical\", \"203.0.113.7\", ClientAddress.parse(\"203.0.113.7\").key()\n                .split(\"/\")[0]);\n        ok(\"a named source is not flagged unknown\", !ClientAddress.parse(\"203.0.113.7\").isUnknown());\n        ok(\"the fallback is flagged unknown\",                + (candidate == null ? \"null\" : describe(candidate).equals(\"U+20203\")\n                            ? \"space\" : candidate.length() > 20 ? \"long\" : candidate),\n                    ClientAddress.parse(candidate) == ClientAddress.UNKNOWN);\n        }\n        ok(\"the unknown bucket is stable\", ClientAddress.parse(\"zzz\").key()\n                .equals(ClientAddress.parse(\"yyy\").key()));\n        eq(\"a null source is bucketed as unknown, never skipped\", ClientAddress.UNKNOWN,\n                ClientAddress.parse(null));\n    }\n\n    // LinkedHashMap<String, String>();\n        single.put(key, value);\n        return single;\n    }\n\n    private static Map<String, String> pair(String k1, String v1, String k2, String v2) {\n        Map<String, String> two = new LinkedHashMap<String, String>();\n        two.put(k1, v1);\n        two.put(k2, v2);\n        return two;\n    }\n\n    private static java.util.function.Function<String, String> mapLookup(final Map<String, String> values) {\n        return new java.util.function.Function<String, String>() {\n            @Override\n            public String apply(String name) {\n                return values.get(name);\n            }\n        };\n    }\n\n    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ bodies\n\n    private static void responseBody() {\n        begin(\"RESPONSE BODIES: constant refusal, no echoed credential, escaped output\");\n        SessionCookiePolicy policy = SessionCookiePolicy.of(null, null, null);\n        String granted = !granted.contains(GOOD));\n        ok(\"refusal body is a fixed string\", ResponseBody.REFUSAL.contains(\"could not complete sign-in\"));\n        String[] leakWords = {\"admin\", \"identifier\", ok(\"refusal body does not mention '\" + word + '\\'',\n                    !ResponseBody.REFUSAL.toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT).contains(word));\n        }\n        eq(\"HTML escaping neutralises markup\", Exception {\n        begin(\"HTTP LAYER: status codes, headers, method handling, fail-closed wiring\");\n        SessionCookiePolicy policy = SessionCookiePolicy.of(null, null, null);\n        CountingVerifier store = new CountingVerifier(GOOD);\n        SessionHandoffServlet serving = new SessionHandoffServlet();\n        serving.configure(new SessionHandoffService(policy, store, new AttemptLimiter(60, 100, 1000, 1000)),\n                new SessionCookieWriter(policy),\n                new RequestAttributeAssertionSource(\"com.acme.test.assertedId\"));\n        ok(\"a fully wired servlet serves\", serving.isServing());\n\n        Recording grantedResponse = Recording.create();\n        serving.doGet(FakeRequest.get(\"203.0.113.5\", \"com.acme.test.assertedId\", GOOD).proxy(),\n                grantedResponse.proxy());\n        eq(\"granted status\", 200, grantedResponse.status);\n        eq(\"one cookie on grant\", 1, grantedResponse.cookies.size());\n        eq(\"cookie value\", GOOD, grantedResponse.cookies.get(0).getValue());\n        eq(\"no-store on grant\", \"no-store, max-age=0\", grantedResponse.header(\"Cache-Control\"));\n        eq(\"nosniff on not contain the identifier\", !grantedResponse.body().contains(GOOD));\n        ok(\"no Set-Cookie in the body\", !grantedResponse.body().toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT)\n                .contains(\"set-cookie\"));\n\n        // Uniform refusals: identical bytes for every reason.\n        Map<String, Recording> refusals = new LinkedHashMap<String, Recording>();\n This is the only class in the component that\n * touches a Servlet API type, so the security decision stays testable without a container.\n *\n * <p>The identifier is re-validated immediately before emission. {@link SessionId} already validated\n * it, but the value crosses a trust boundary at this line: a later maintainer could introduce a path\n * that hands this writer an identifier from somewhere else. The response is therefore only mutated\n * after the second check passes, and the check is reject-only (no normalisation), so a rejected value\n * cannot reach the response at all.\n */\npublic final class SessionCookieWriter {\n\n    private static final String SAME_SITE_ATTRIBUTE = \"SameSite\";\n\n    /** Any response that can carry session material is uncacheable, without exception. */\n    private static final String NO_STORE = \"no-store, max-age=0\";\n\n    private final SessionCookiePolicy policy;\n\n    public SessionCookieWriter(SessionCookiePolicy policy) {\n        if (policy == null) {\n            throw new IllegalArgumentException(\"cookie policy is required\");\n        }\n        this.policy = policy;\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Writes the anti-caching headers and then the {@code Set-Cookie} header. Nothing else.\n     *\n     * <p>{@code no-store} is set first so that if the cookie write below somehow fails, the partial\n     * response that reaches the network is already uncacheable. Both must precede the first body byte:\n     * a servlet container silently discards headers set afterwards.\n     *\n     * @param sessionIdentifier identifier already accepted by the trusted session owner\n     * @param response          response to mutate\n     * @throws InvalidSessionIdentifierException if the identifier is not a well-formed token; the\n     *         response then carries the cache headers and no cookie\n     */\n    public void writeSessionCookie(SessionId sessionIdentifier, HttpServletResponse response)\n            throws InvalidSessionIdentifierException {\n        if (response == null) {\n            throw new IllegalArgumentException(\"response is required\");\n        }\n        // Unconditional and first: a response that carried, failed to carry, or partially carried\n        // session material must never be storable by a browser or an intermediary.\n        response.setHeader(\"Cache-Control\", NO_STORE);\n        response.setHeader(\"Pragma\", \"no-cache\");\n        if (sessionIdentifier == null) {\n            throw new InvalidSessionIdentifierException(SessionId.Rejection.ABSENT);\n        }\n        String value = sessionIdentifier.value();\n        SessionId.Rejection rejection = SessionId.inspect(value);\n        if (rejection != SessionId.Rejection.NONE) {\n            // The reason class is safe to log. The value is interpolated nowhere below.\n            throw new InvalidSessionIdentifierException(rejection);\n        }\n\n        Cookie cookie = new Cookie(policy.name(), value);\n        cookie.setPath(policy.path());\n        cookie.setHttpOnly(policy.httpOnly());\n        cookie.setSecure(policy.secure());\n        // setMaxAge is deliberately never called. Tomcat renders maxAge == 0 as\n        // \"Expires=Tue Nov 17 10:15:05 GMT 1995\", an already-expired cookie the browser discards, so\n        // a session cookie must keep the API default of emitting no expiry attribute at all.\n        // Servlet 6.0 has no SameSite setter; the attribute map is the supported extension point and\n        // Tomcat 10.1 renders it into Set-Cookie. It receives a session identifier that\nan upstream trusted component already created and validated server-side, and returns it to the\nbrowser in a session cookie. Nothing else: it does not authenticate, does not create sessions, does\nnot read or write a container-managed session, and does not authorise anything.\n\nEverything below is written against the eight review rules in `prompt.txt`, which are quoted in the\nsame order in [Rule by rule](#rule-by-rule-how-the-code-satisfies-each-of-the-eight-rules).\n\n```\nsrc/main/java/com/acme/portal/session/   16 classes, 2262 lines  <- the component\nsrc/test/java/com/acme/portal/session/Harness.java                <- 346 in-process checks\nsrc/test/java/com/acme/portal/testapp/                            <- stand-ins used only by the e2e run\ndeploy/web.xml                                                    <- descriptor a deployment copies\ntools/mutants.py                                                  <- 32-mutant battery\nbuild.sh                                                          <- build + harness + 3 real-HTTP modes\n```\n\n## What goes on the wire\n\nOne successful response, one refusal body, one limit status:\n\n```\nHTTP/1.1 200\nCache-Control: no-store, max-age=0\nPragma: no-cache\nX-Content-Type-Options: nosniff\nContent-Type: text/html;charset=UTF-8\nSet-Cookie: __Host-PORTAL_SESSION=xkQfX0Zd2Y4_VtXeJV87p3KHlOek9CZWvTlqLUj8Vzs; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict\n```\n\nThat line is copied from `build/logs/e2e-default.log`, i.e. it is what Tomcat 10.1.60 actually put on\na socket, not what the code asked for. No `Max-Age` and no `Expires`: `setMaxAge` is never called,\nbecause a browser-session cookie must carry neither attribute (Tomcat renders `maxAge == 0` as an\nalready-past `Expires`, which silently kills the cookie). No `Domain` either — `setDomain` is never\ncalled, which is what makes the `__Host-` prefix hold (host-only, `Path=/`, `Secure`).\n\n| Response | When | Body |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `200` + cookie | the verifier confirmed the identifier (GET) | constant \"signed in\" page |\n| `200` no cookie, no `Set-Cookie` | same decision, `HEAD` | none, `Content-Length` of the GET body |\n| `403` | no assertion, malformed assertion, store says no, verifier threw | one constant refusal page |\n| `429` + `Retry-After` | per-source, global or tracking-state limit hit | the same refusal page |\n| `503` + `Retry-After: 5` | not wired, no verifier deployed, bad settings, unsafe deployment, internal error | the same refusal page |\n| `405` + `Allow` | POST/PUT/DELETE/OPTIONS | none |\n| `501` + `Allow` | TRACE | none |\n\n## Run it\n\n```sh\n./build.sh --unit     # compile + the 346-check in-process harness\n./build.sh            # the above, then deploy to a throwaway Tomcat and assert over real HTTP\npython3 tools/mutants.py --run --jobs 4 --max-jvms 2\n```\n\n`build.sh` needs the JDK and the two pinned third-party files listed under\n[Rule 8](#8-prefer-the-platform-name-versions-verify-downloads-never-load-code-from-shared-places);\nit refuses to compile or extract if either file's checksum does not match. Logs land in\n`build/logs/`. The three end-to-end modes each start their own Tomcat on a port pair taken from\ndisjoint ranges and shut it down again (`/proc/net/tcp` LISTEN rows are checked before and after —\nthere is no `ss`/`netstat`/`lsof`/`ps` on this machine).\n\n## Threat model, stated plainly\n\nThe task says the identifier is produced by another component, which collides head-on with rule 4\n(\"session identifiers must be generated by this code — never accepted from the caller\"). That\ncollision is the whole design problem, and it is resolved like this:\n\nThe incoming value is treated as an **assertion**, not as an identifier. An assertion is\nunvalidated bytes that happen to come from inside the JVM, and it gets exactly the treatment rule 4\ndemands of anything this code did not mint:\n\n1. Strict, **reject-only** validation ([`SessionId.inspect`](src/main/java/com/acme/portal/session/SessionId.java))\n   before anything else touches it.\n2. Mandatory re-check against server-side state through a `SessionStateVerifier` that this component\n   does not implement — the application supplies it via `ServiceLoader`, and if it is absent,\n   ambiguous, or throws, the answer is *no*.\n3. A second independent validation gate at the moment of cookie emission\n   ([`SessionCookieWriter`](src/main/java/com/acme/portal/session/SessionCookieWriter.java)), so a\n   future path that reaches the writer by another route still cannot emit an unvalidated value.\n4. `SessionId.generate()` — the component's own 256-bit CSPRNG path — exists, is tested, and is what\n   a deployment that *can* mint its own identifiers should use. It is not used for the handoff,\n   because handing out a freshly minted id for an asserted one would create a second session\n   mechanism.\n\n**Residual risk, which no validation in this file removes:** if the upstream authenticator can be\ntricked into asserting an identifier that belongs to somebody else, this component will correctly\nverify that the session exists and correctly set the cookie — for the attacker. The trust placed in\nthe authenticator is real and cannot be validated from here. What limits the blast radius:\n\n- The assertion attribute is read **only** as a `String` set by server-side code in the same JVM.\n  The reader never looks at cookies, query parameters, body fields, or any header, so a client\n  cannot name the attribute it wants copied into a cookie.\n- Anything that *can* set a request attribute in that JVM can already act as the user; the component\n  adds no new way to reach them.\n- The value never lands in a URL, a log line, a body, a file, or `toString()` — so handing it to the\n  browser is the only disclosure path, and the browser is the intended recipient.\n- Deployment requirement: the filter that sets the attribute must be mapped to this servlet's exact\n  path, must run before it, and nothing upstream may copy client data into that attribute.\n\n`X-Forwarded-For` and every other `*-For` header are **never read**. `ClientAddress` keys the limiter\non `request.getRemoteAddr()` alone. Behind a proxy that field is the proxy's address, so every\nclient shares one bucket — a availability annoyance, never an authorisation decision. Reading\n`X-Forwarded-For` instead would hand the attacker the choice of rate-limit bucket, i.e. a way to\nframe another source. If a deployment *must* key limits on the real client, the proxy has to\noverwrite a single well-known header and the change belongs in `ClientAddress`, which is the only\nclass that names a source.\n\n## Rule by rule: how the code satisfies each of the eight rules\n\n### 1. Trust boundaries — every input enumerated and validated\n\n| Input | Origin | Validation | Failure |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| asserted session identifier | server-side attribute set by the authenticator | length 32–128, base64url charset only, ≥ 12 distinct chars, then verifier | `403`, comparable work |\n| HTTP method | client | only GET/HEAD have a decision path | `405`, `501` for TRACE |\n| request URI / context path | client | never parsed; servlet mapping decides | — |\n| `remoteAddr` | container | hex digits, `.` and `:` only; dotted-quad or IPv6 shape; then JDK parser | shared `unknown/0` bucket |\n| `If-None-Match` | client | read by the container only; this code never branches on it (a conditional grant is a full `200`) | — |\n| cookies, query params, body, all `*-For` headers | client | **never read** | — |\n| 8 environment variables | operator / deployer | integer ranges, name/path charsets, SameSite enum, relation `perWindow ≤ global` | `503` for every request |\n| `META-INF/services` provider | application deployment | exactly one, constructible, plus its code-source hygiene | `503` for every request |\n| `web.xml` | operator | mapped to one exact path, `tracking-mode COOKIE`, error pages routed to a static file | deploy-time |\n| code-source locations on the classpath | filesystem | POSIX `OTHERS_WRITE` must be absent, on this class *and* the verifier's class | `503` for every request |\n| clock | `System.currentTimeMillis` via an injectable `AttemptLimiter.Clock` | window rolls are recomputed per call, never trusted from a stored count | conservative (limits earlier) |\n\nTwo decisions in that table are load-bearing and deliberate:\n\n- **Nothing is normalised.** No `trim()`, no case folding, no unescaping. `String.trim()` deletes\n  every character ≤ U+0020 — including NUL and tab — so `\"abc…\\t\"` and `\"abc…\"` would become the\n  same session for two different inputs. Validation refuses such values instead of repairing them.\n- **No client value decides a security outcome.** `remoteAddr` only chooses a rate-limit bucket; a\n  wrong or forged address costs the attacker a slower retry, never access.\n\nThe `SessionId.inspect` character loop also carries a bound check that is unreachable today, because\nthe allowlist refuses every character at or above the table size. It stays: the array bound depends\non the allowlist, and widening the accepted charset without it turns a long input into an\n`ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException` triggered by attacker-supplied data (a `500` on demand). The\n`SID-charset` mutant in the battery exists precisely to prove that line is load-bearing.\n\n### 2. Secrets — none embedded, and the one this code handles is never printable\n\nThere is no credential, key or password anywhere in `src/main` or `deploy`. The bearer credential is\nthe session identifier itself, and the design assumption is that *any* text path can leak it, so the\ntype itself refuses to render it:\n\n- `SessionId.toString()` returns `SessionId(<12 hex chars of a domain-separated SHA-256>)`, never the\n  value. A `log.warn(\"id=\" + id)` or a `%s` in someone else's exception message cannot disclose it.\n- `SessionId.value()` is **package private**: code outside `com.acme.portal.session` cannot obtain the\n  raw string to write it somewhere else.\n- No log statement in the component interpolates an identifier or a client address. The only\n  identifier ever logged is the fingerprint; the only limiter detail logged is an outcome enum plus a\n  boolean (\"was the source unknown\").\n- Exception paths log `exceptionType=<class name>` only. A JDBC or datastore message can carry a\n  connection string, and this component will not put one on a log it does not own.\n- Nothing is written to a file, to `argv`, to a URL, or to the response body. The e2e suite asserts\n  the credential appears in `Set-Cookie` and nowhere else in the response, including the body.\n- `equals`/`hashCode` are deliberately **not** implemented on `SessionId`: comparing bearer\n  credentials is a timing channel, and this component never needs to compare one (it never reads a\n  cookie back).\n\n### 3. Authentication and access — verified against state, failing closed, throttled both ways\n\n`SessionHandoffService.handle` is the only decision, and every one of its exits is a refusal except\none:\n\n```java\nboolean valid;\ntry {\n    valid = verifier.isSessionValid(sessionId.value());\n} catch (RuntimeException verifierFailed) {\n    valid = false;                    // could not confirm == \"no\"\n}\nif (!valid) { return new Decision(Outcome.REFUSED_UNAUTHENTICATED, null, 0); }\n```\n\nThere is no `if (verifier == null) allow`, no feature flag, no \"assume the filter was right\". The\nfail-closed ladder in `SessionHandoffServlet.init()` covers the ways a verifier can be *missing*\nrather than wrong — invalid settings, hygiene problem, provider load failure, no provider, more than\none provider (it refuses to guess which store is authoritative), and partially wired collaborators.\nEvery one ends in `serveNothing()`, and `serving == false` answers `503` for 100% of requests. A\nservlet that cannot check is not a servlet that skips checking.\n\nThrottling, [`AttemptLimiter`](src/main/java/com/acme/portal/session/AttemptLimiter.java):\n\n- **Per source and globally**, both checked, both in one monitor.\n- **Refusals consume nothing.** A malformed or unverifiable assertion returns before the budget is\n  touched, so an attacker cannot spend a victim's allowance with garbage. Verified over real HTTP by\n  the `limited` mode: six free refusals stay `403`, and the grant count afterwards is exactly the\n  configured allowance.\n- **Global saturation is checked before the per-source counter increments**, so a flood that\n  saturates the shared lane cannot lock out the clients that never sent it — the rule's \"an attacker\n  cannot use your own limit to lock a legitimate user out\", applied to the global limit too.\n- **The unknown-source bucket is smaller** (`max(1, perSource / 4)`), because \"I could not establish\n  your address\" is the shape an attacker forges.\n- Bucket state is bounded (`PORTAL_HANDOFF_MAX_TRACKED_SOURCES`, default 200 000, roll-based\n  eviction; when eviction cannot free space the answer is `429`, not unbounded memory).\n- No account lockout exists here at all: this component has no account concept, and the limiter only\n  delays retries.\n\n### 4. Identifiers and tokens — CSPRNG, strict validation, documented residual risk, cookie attributes\n\n- `SessionId.generate()`: 32 bytes from a shared `SecureRandom` → 43 unpadded base64url characters =\n  256 bits. `getInstanceStrong()` is avoided deliberately (it can block a request thread); the shared\n  instance is the platform-recommended pattern and reseeds from the OS source. The generated value is\n  fed back through `inspect()` — if our own encoder ever produces something this class rejects, the\n  component refuses to serve rather than hand out an identifier nobody can use.\n- The externally provided identifier is validated as above and its residual risk is documented in\n  both the javadoc and [the threat model](#threat-model-stated-plainly).\n- Cookie attributes are invariants, not configuration:\n  - `HttpOnly` and `Secure` are hard-coded `true` in `SessionCookiePolicy`; the settings loader has no\n    path that sets them false (`POLICY-secure-hardcoded`, `POLICY-httpOnly-hardcoded` mutants).\n  - `SameSite` accepts only `Strict` or `Lax`; **`None` is refused at construction** because it is\n    meaningless without `Secure` and is the cross-site-leak setting. Set through\n    `Cookie#setAttribute` because Servlet 6.0 has no SameSite setter (6.1 added one); Tomcat renders it.\n  - Path must start with `/`, is charset-allowlisted and length-bounded; a `__Host-` name paired with\n    any path other than `/` is refused at startup rather than producing a cookie the browser silently\n    drops.\n  - Cookie *name* is allowlisted, cannot start with a digit, cannot collide with a protocol keyword\n    (`set-cookie`, `domain`, `expires`, …), and is length-bounded — the defaults are the safe ones.\n  - No `Max-Age`/`Expires` ever ⇒ browser-session lifetime.\n- 403/429/503 responses carry no `Set-Cookie` at all — asserted in-process and over HTTP.\n\n### 5. Sensitive data — masked, bounded, private, with an honest note on \"cleared from memory\"\n\n- **Masked:** fingerprinting as in rule 2; the refusal page is a constant with no echoed input; the\n  one dynamic string that does reach HTML goes through `ResponseBody.escapeHtml`, which escapes the\n  markup characters and turns control characters (including NUL) into spaces, bounded at 256 bytes.\n- **Bounded stored size:** the only thing this component stores is rate-limit counters — one\n  `{count, windowStart}` per canonical source key, at most `maxTrackedSources` keys, each canonical\n  key at most 64 characters. No identifier, address or payload is ever retained past the request.\n- **Private file modes:** the component writes no files. It additionally refuses to *start* if its\n  own code source or the verifier's is world-writable (`DeploymentHygiene`, POSIX `OTHERS_WRITE`), and\n  fails closed on a filesystem whose permissions it cannot judge — that is rule 8's \"never load code\n  from a shared place\" enforced at runtime rather than left to a runbook. Test scratch directories are\n  created per PID and removed by a shutdown hook (not at the end of `main`, which the failure paths\n  never reach).\n- **\"Clear credentials from memory when done\" — the honest version.** The JVM cannot honour this for a\n  `String`, and this task's input *is* a `String` handed over by another component. `String` is\n  immutable, its value is not zeroable, garbage collection decides when the memory is reusable, and\n  the JIT may intern or copy it. Pretending otherwise would be the kind of claim a reviewer is right\n  to report. What the code actually does, and the most that is achievable here:\n  - the fewest possible copies: `CacheSupport.digestHexPrefix` feeds the digest from the parts\n    without materialising `prefix + secret`, and truncates during formatting rather than building a\n    64-character digest string and cutting it;\n  - every intermediate *it* allocates is zeroed on the way out (`byte[]`, `char[]`, digest output);\n  - the copy it does not own is not extended: no cache holds it, no field outside the request-scoped\n    `SessionId` does, and `value()` is package private so nothing else can retain it casually.\n  A deployment that must bound credential lifetime at the byte level needs the platform's\n  char[]-based APIs (`PBEKeySpec`, `SecretKeySpec`) on the *producer* side, which is the authenticator,\n  not this component.\n\n### 6. Failure behaviour — identical messages, comparable work, no permissive default\n\n- **One** refusal body for `403`, `429` and `503`. The harness asserts every refusal path renders\n  byte-identical output and that the set of distinct refusal bodies has exactly one member.\n- **No existence oracle.** `403` means \"no session was issued to you\", which is true and already\n  observable from the missing cookie; it never says whether the identifier was absent, malformed,\n  unknown, or rejected by a broken verifier. The distinction *does* exist internally (`Outcome`) and\n  goes only to the log, at `INFO`, as an enum name.\n- **Comparable work.** `WorkEqualizer.apply()` runs 200 chained SHA-256 compressions on **every**\n  request, before the decision and on all five measured paths. Padding only the refusal paths is not\n  enough: the `503` availability path short-circuits before them, and a path that costs nothing next\n  to one that costs 90 µs is itself the \"does this session exist\" oracle. Measured in µs (in ms every\n  path prints \"1 ms\"):\n\n  ```\n  granted              p50=99 us      no assertion         p50=98 us\n  malformed assertion  p50=99 us      unknown session      p50=98 us\n  not serving          p50=73 us      spread=1.36x  equalizerCompressions=200\n  ```\n\n  The suite asserts an absolute floor (≥ 60 µs) as well as the ratio: a mutant that removes the\n  padding from *all* branches keeps the spread at 1.0 and would sail through a ratio-only assertion.\n- **Unknown input is rejected, never substituted.** Bad settings do not fall back to defaults — they\n  stop the component. A non-`String` assertion attribute is \"no assertion\" rather than\n  `toString()`-ed. An unparseable address is the shared restricted bucket rather than an anonymous\n  unlimited one. A verifier that throws is \"no\". `SC_TOO_MANY_REQUESTS` does not exist in Servlet 6.0,\n  so 429 is declared locally rather than approximated with 403.\n- **Errors to the client stay generic; detail goes to the log.** No exception escapes this servlet —\n  the container's error page would print class names, messages and stack, and `deploy/web.xml` routes\n  `404`/`500`/`Throwable` to a static page with no request data regardless.\n\n### 7. Concurrency — check-and-act is atomic\n\n`AttemptLimiter.tryAcquire` reads the bucket, rolls it if stale, checks both ceilings, and increments\nboth counters inside a single `synchronized (monitor)` block. There is no window where two threads\ncan both observe `count == ceiling - 1` and both grant.\n\nOrdering inside that block is a security property, not style: the global ceiling is checked *before*\nthe per-source increment (a saturated shared lane must not spend an innocent source's allowance), and\nbudget acquisition happens *before* the verifier call, so a slow store cannot be used to pile up\nin-flight requests that all later pass.\n\n`SessionHandoffService` is immutable after wiring, `ClientAddress` is immutable, `SessionId` is\nimmutable, and the servlet's collaborator fields are written once in `init`/`configure`. The one\n`ThreadLocal<MessageDigest>` is confined to `CacheSupport` and `reset()` in a `finally`.\n\nThe harness runs the limiter from concurrent threads against one bucket and asserts the total grants\nequal the ceiling exactly — the assertion that dies first if the `synchronized` block is removed.\n\n### 8. Prefer the platform; name versions; verify downloads; never load code from shared places\n\nNothing hand-rolled where the platform suffices:\n\n| Need | Used instead of |\n| --- | --- |\n| cookie syntax/attributes | `jakarta.servlet.http.Cookie` + `response.addCookie`, not `setHeader(\"Set-Cookie\", …)` |\n| CSPRNG | `java.security.SecureRandom` (OS-backed), not `Random`/`Math.random`/time |\n| digest | `MessageDigest.getInstance(\"SHA-256\")` (JCA), not a private SHA |\n| verifier discovery | `ServiceLoader`, not reflection on a hard-coded class name |\n| base64url | `java.util.Base64.getUrlEncoder().withoutPadding()` |\n| session-id-in-URL | `session-config/tracking-mode COOKIE` so the container cannot append `;jsessionid=` |\n| TLS/HSTS | deliberately **not** claimed in `web.xml`: no keystore here means a `transport-guarantee` element would be decoration. The cookie is `Secure` regardless, so a plain-HTTP deployment stops working rather than leaking. |\n\nPinned third-party files, both under `tools/`, both verified by `build.sh` before use, both from the\nofficial publisher:\n\n| Artifact | Version | Source | Verification |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| `jakarta.servlet-api-6.0.0.jar` | Jakarta Servlet 6.0.0 | `https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/jakarta/servlet/jakarta.servlet-api/6.0.0/` | publisher's `.sha1` = `abecc699286e65035ebba9844c03931357a6a963`; locally pinned SHA-512 `b810ce04…c0c9d5` |\n| `apache-tomcat-10.1.60.tar.gz` | Tomcat 10.1.60 | `https://downloads.apache.org/tomcat/tomcat-10/v10.1.60/bin/` | pinned SHA-512 `aa065083…61bd04`, `sha512sum -c` OK |\n\nNotes that a reviewer should not have to rediscover:\n\n- Maven Central publishes only `.sha1` for the servlet API artifact. A `.sha512` fetched from it is a\n  404 HTML page — which is exactly what one of these files contained before it was deleted. So the\n  SHA-512 pin is named `*.pinned-sha512`: it records *this project's* expected digest, not a publisher\n  signature, and the README says so rather than implying a provenance it does not have.\n- The published `.sha1` holds a bare digest with no filename, which `sha1sum -c` refuses to parse, so\n  `build.sh` compares the digests directly and rejects an empty or truncated signature file by length.\n- Both gates were negative-tested: an appended byte in the jar, an emptied `.sha1`, and an appended\n  byte in the Tomcat archive each make `build.sh` exit `2` before compiling or extracting.\n- Toolchain actually used: OpenJDK `17.0.20.1` (`javac -Xlint:all -Werror -encoding US-ASCII`),\n  GNU bash, python3 (gates and battery only). Platform encoding here is US-ASCII, so non-ASCII Java\n  sources would not compile — hence the explicit `-encoding` and the ASCII byte gate.\n- Code loaded from shared or world-writable places is refused at runtime, not just in prose — see\n  `DeploymentHygiene` under [rule 5](#5-sensitive-data-masked-bounded-private-with-an-honest-note-on-cleared-from-memory).\n\n## What the verification actually proved\n\n| Suite | Checks | Result |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| in-process harness (`build/logs/harness.log`) | 346 | 0 failures |\n| e2e `default` — real Tomcat, real socket | 95 | 0 failures |\n| e2e `limited` — 3 s window, 3 per source | 16 | 0 failures |\n| e2e `noverifier` — no provider deployed | 11 | 0 failures |\n| **total** | **468** | **0 failures** |\n\nHarness sections and their check counts, as printed by the run: identifier validation 49, masking 10,\ngeneration 5, cookie policy 37, cookie writer 26, handoff decision 21, attempt limiter 31, client\naddress 38, settings 28, response bodies 19, HTTP layer 72, deployment hygiene 6, timing 4.\n\nThe servlet API is faked with `java.lang.reflect.Proxy`, so the in-process suite proves what the\ncomponent *asked for*; the e2e modes prove what a real container then put on the wire — which is the\nonly thing a browser sees. Raw-socket assertions are written by hand (the JDK `HttpClient` refuses to\nsend CR/LF inside a header value, which is the exact byte sequence under test).\n\n### Mutation battery: 32 mutants, 32 killed by a real assertion\n\n`python3 tools/mutants.py --run --jobs 4 --max-jvms 2` — the final cycle:\n\n```\nSUMMARY   mutants=32 seconds=214 killed(assert)=32\nACCOUNTED mutants=32 assertion-kills=32 build-failures=0 needs-attention=0\n```\n\nEach mutant is one semantic edit to a frozen copy of `src/main` (the real sources are never touched;\n`--dry` verifies every anchor matches exactly once before a cycle is spent). The tests are frozen\nwhile a battery runs, so a mutant cannot be killed by editing the test that was supposed to catch it.\n\nAccounting is deliberately strict, because a green battery is worthless if a crash counts as a kill:\n\n- `killed(assert)` — the harness printed at least one `FAILED` line. **All 32.**\n- `killed(build)` — reported separately; a mutant that does not compile proves the edit was illegal,\n  not that a guard is tested. **0 this cycle.**\n- `harness-error` — exit ≠ 0 with no `FAILED` line, i.e. a crash. **0 this cycle.** Getting there took\n  two real fixes: `SID-charset` used to crash the harness with `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`, which\n  was a genuine product fragility (now refused in `SessionId.inspect`), and the harness now wraps each\n  section so an abort becomes a named failed check instead of an anonymous stack trace.\n- Two mutants were initially *equivalent* and are documented as such rather than forced into a kill:\n  `SVC-null-verifier` renamed a private field (an NPE that the existing `catch (RuntimeException)`\n  already treats as \"no\"), and `BODY-constant-refusal` renamed a constant. Both were replaced with\n  edits that weaken behaviour — an always-true verifier, and un-escaped HTML output.\n- Two survivors were **real test gaps**, found and closed rather than accepted:\n  - `ADDR-allowlist` survived because every garbage entry in the list was already refused by the\n    shape check, so nothing depended on the character allowlist. The added assertions name the\n    distinctive failures instead: `InetAddress.getByName(\"fe80::1%9\")` **succeeds**, so without the\n    allowlist each numeric interface-scope id is its own lane; `getByName(\"localhost\")` resolves, so\n    a hostname becomes a DNS query and a private bucket.\n  - `SRV-not-serving` survived because deleting the guard turns the null collaborator into an\n    exception, which the catch-all answers with the same `503` — the two guards are redundant and a\n    status-code test cannot tell them apart. The gap is now observable two ways: the not-serving\n    refusal must log **zero** SEVERE records (deleting the guard makes every request a logged server\n    error — a false alarm and a log-volume amplifier), and an unwired servlet is built as a *never\n    configured* object rather than by calling `configure(null, null, null)`, plus three new checks\n    that any partial collaborator set leaves the servlet refusing. A `SRV-serve-partial` mutant\n    (forcing `complete = true`) now dies on those.\n\n## Deploying it\n\n1. Refuses the\n     * shorthand forms {@code InetAddress} tolerates, so one host cannot open several buckets for one\n     * address by varying how it is written.\n     */\n    private static boolean isDottedQuad(String text) {\n        int groups = 0;\n        int digits = 0;\n        int value = 0;\n        for (int i = 0; i < text.length(); i++) {\n            char c = text.charAt(i);\n            if (c == '.') {\n                if (digits == 0 || digits > 3 || value > 255) {\n                    return false;\n                }\n                groups++;\n                digits = 0;\n                value = 0;\n            } else if (c >= '0' && c <= '9') {\n                // A leading zero is tolerated in text but the numeric bound below is what matters.\n                digits++;\n                value = value * 10 + (c - '0');\n            } else {\n                return false;\n            }\n        }\n        if (digits == 0 || digits > 3 || value > 255) {\n            return false;\n        }\n        groups++;\n        return groups == 4;\n    }\n\n    /** True when the dotted part of a mixed form such as {@code ::ffff:1.2.3.4} is a real quad. */\n    private static boolean hasEmbeddedIpv4(String text) {\n        int lastColon = text.lastIndexOf(':');\n        return lastColon >= 0 && isDottedQuad(text.substring(lastColon + 1));\n    }\n\n    private final String canonical;\n    private final int prefixBits;\n    private final boolean unknown;\n\n    private ClientAddress(String canonical, int prefixBits, boolean unknown) {\n        this.canonical = canonical;\n        this.prefixBits = prefixBits;\n        this.unknown = unknown;\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Parses and canonicalises a textual address.\n     *\n     * <p>The shape is checked before the JDK parser is consulted, because\n     * {@code InetAddress.getByName} also accepts {@code 517996801}, {@code 0x7f.1}, {@code 10.1} and\n     * similar shorthand forms. A container never emits those, and admitting them would mean one host\n     * could hold several buckets for the same address purely by textual form -- the exact unfairness\n     * this class exists to prevent.\n     *\n     * @return the canonical form, or {@link #UNKNOWN} for absent, oversized, non-textual or\n     *         unparseable input. No exception is thrown: a malformed address must degrade to a\n     *         shared limited bucket, never to an unlimited one, and never to a stack trace.\n     */\n    public static ClientAddress parse(String remoteAddr) {\n        if (remoteAddr == null || remoteAddr.isEmpty() || remoteAddr.length() > MAX_RAW_LENGTH) {\n            return UNKNOWN;\n        }\n        // Reject structural surprises before the parser sees them, so no bracket, scope-id,\n        // percent-encoding or control character can reach InetAddress parsing.\n        for (int i = 0; i < remoteAddr.length(); i++) {\n            char c = remoteAddr.charAt(i);\n            boolean allowed = (c >= '0' && c <= '9') || (c >= 'a' && c <= 'f') || (c >= 'A' && c <= 'F')\n                    || c == '.' || c == ':';\n            if (!allowed) {\n                return UNKNOWN;\n            }\n        }\n        boolean ipv6 = remoteAddr.indexOf(':') >= 0;\n        if (ipv6) {\n            if (remoteAddr.length() > MAX_IPV6_LENGTH) {\n                return UNKNOWN;\n            }\n            if (remoteAddr.indexOf('.') >= 0 && !hasEmbeddedIpv4(remoteAddr)) {\n                return UNKNOWN;\n            }\n        } else if (!isDottedQuad(remoteAddr)) {\n            return UNKNOWN;\n        }\n        InetAddress address;\n        try {\n            // getByName consults the resolver for a hostname. i < 10; i++) {\n            if (bytes[i] != 0) {\n                return false;\n            }\n        }\n        boolean mapped = bytes[10] == (byte) 0xFF && bytes[11] == (byte) 0xFF;\n        boolean compatible = bytes[10] == 0 && bytes[11] == 0;\n        return mapped || compatible;\n    }\n\n    /** Lower-case canonical text of the top 64 bits, e.g. {@code 2001:db8:0:1}. */\n    private static String canonicalIpv6Prefix(byte[] bytes) {\n        StringBuilder text = new StringBuilder(19);\n        for (int group = 0; correct component into remote\n * code execution: loading classes from somewhere another local account can write.\n *\n * <p>The component reads no files itself, so file permissions would be moot if it stayed alone. But\n * it does one thing that pulls the environment in: it discovers the application's session verifier\n * through a service loader, and a loader follows the classpath. If any location on that path is\n * writable by another account, that account can supply the code that answers \"is this session\n * valid\", and every guard in this package becomes decoration. Rule 8 asks for exactly this check, so\n * it is performed and enforced rather than assumed.\n *\n * <p>What is inspected: every JVM classpath entry, plus the code-source location (and its parent\n * directory, because a writable directory lets a file be replaced even when the file is not) of this\n * class and of the resolved verifier -- the two code bases that actually decide the outcome.\n *\n * <p>Descriptions name a path and nothing else. Paths are configuration, not secrets, and the text\n * stays terse because it reaches a log line.\n */\nfinal class DeploymentHygiene {\n\n    private static final int MAX_ENTRIES = 512;\n    private static final int MAX_PATH_LENGTH = 4096;\n\n    private DeploymentHygiene() {\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @param codeOwners classes whose own code location must be trustworthy; typically this class and\n     *                   the resolved session verifier\n     * @return {@code null} when the deployment looks safe, otherwise a one-line reason to refuse\n     *         service. An unreadable location is reported as a problem: \"unknown\" is not \"safe\".\n     */\n    static String describeProblem(Class<?>... codeOwners) {\n        Set<Path> locations = new LinkedHashSet<Path>();\n        String classpath = System.getProperty(\"java.class.path\", \"\");\n        if (!classpath.isEmpty()) {\n            String[] entries = classpath.split(File.pathSeparator);\n            if (entries.length > MAX_ENTRIES) {\n                return \"the JVM classpath has more than \" + MAX_ENTRIES + \" entries\";\n            }\n            for (String entry : entries) {\n                Path path = toPath(entry);\n                if (path != null) {\n                    locations.add(path);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        for (Class<?> codeOwner : codeOwners) {\n            if (codeOwner == null) {\n                return \"a required code owner was not supplied\";\n            }\n            Path fromCodeSource = codeSourceLocation(codeOwner);\n            if (fromCodeSource == null) {\n                // Cannot establish where this class was loaded from, so cannot prove it is not\n                // somebody else's to write. Unknown is not safe.\n                return \"the code location of \" + codeOwner.getName() + \" could not be established\";\n            }\n            locations.add(fromCodeSource);\n        }\n        for (Path location : locations) {\n            if (!Files.exists(location)) {\n                continue;\n            }\n            if (worldWritable(location)) {\n                return \"code is loadable from a location other users can write: \" + location;\n            }\n            Path parent = location.getParent();\n            if (parent != null && Files.isDirectory(parent) && worldWritable(parent)) {\n                return \"code is loadable from a directory other users can write: \" + parent;\n            }\n        }\n        return null;\n    }\n\n    private static Path toPath(String entry) {\n        if (entry == null || entry.isEmpty() || entry.length() > MAX_PATH_LENGTH) {\n            return null;\n        }\n        try {\n            return Paths.get(entry);\n        } catch (RuntimeException | Error unparseable) {\n            return null;\n        }\n    }\n\n    private static Path codeSourceLocation(Class<?> owner) {\n        try {\n            ProtectionDomain domain = owner.getProtectionDomain();\n            CodeSource source = domain == null ? null : domain.getCodeSource();\n            if (source == null || source.getLocation() == null) {\n                return null;\n            }\n            java.net.URL location = source.getLocation();\n            if (!\"file\".equalsIgnoreCase(location.getProtocol())) {\n                // A jar over http or a nested module location cannot be judged by POSIX bits, and\n                // neither is a directory an attacker could have written in place.\n                return null;\n            }\n            return toPath(java.net.URLDecoder.decode(location.getPath(),\n                    java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets.UTF_8));\n        } catch (RuntimeException | Error unavailable) {\n            return null;\n        }\n    }\n\n    private static boolean worldWritable(Path path) {\n        try {\n            Set<java.nio.file.attribute.PosixFilePermission> permissions =\n                    Files.getPosixFilePermissions(path);\n            return permissions.contains(java.nio.file.attribute.PosixFilePermission.OTHERS_WRITE);\n        } catch (UnsupportedOperationException notPosix) {\n            // A filesystem without POSIX bits cannot be judged here. com.acme.portal.session;\n\n/**\n * Does a fixed, small amount of throwaway computation on every request.\n *\n * <p><b>What it equalizes.</b> A refusal that happens <i>before</i> the session-store lookup is\n * measurably cheaper than one that happens after it. The response body already hides which check\n * refused, but latency does not: an attacker who can time the endpoint can tell \"this candidate is\n * not even well-formed\" from \"this candidate is well-formed but unknown\", which is a per-candidate\n * signal for anyone generating identifiers. Padding every outcome to the cost of the most expensive\n * one removes that signal.\n *\n * <p>The work is a fixed number of SHA-256 compressions over a constant buffer: no secret, no\n * attacker-controlled length, no I/O, and a cost independent of every input, which is what makes it\n * a level playing field rather than a new side channel.\n *\n * <p><b>Why it runs before every gate, including the throttle.</b> A cheap path is itself a signal,\n * so the padding is applied first and unconditionally. That costs something real, and it is a trade\n * rather than a free win: a request the rate limiter refuses still pays for the padding, so the\n * limiter sheds the session-store round trip and the cookie write, not this. Moving the padding off\n * the limited path would make \"you are being throttled for this address\" readable as a latency\n * difference, and would leave the availability refusal as a cheap probe for whether this deployment\n * is wired up at all. The accepted trade is therefore explicit -- constant work on every path, and a\n * constant small enough that this is a capacity cost of tens of microseconds rather than the lever a\n * flooding attacker would rather press.\n *\n * <p>The count was measured on this machine, not guessed: see the harness {@code TIMING} section,\n * which prints per-outcome microsecond timings and asserts both an absolute floor and a spread bound.\n * A padding constant that is never measured is how a guard like this silently stops working: if the\n * padding is smaller than the difference it is meant to hide, deleting it changes nothing observable\n * and no test can notice.\n */\nfinal class WorkEqualizer {\n\n    /**\n     * SHA-256 compressions per request. Cost here is about {@code 3 us + 0.38 us x n}, so 48 lands\n     * near 21 us -- but the harness measures the call in the same run that checks it, so neither\n     * figure is taken on trust.\n     *\n     * <p>The sizing is two-sided because the guard fails in both directions. Rejecting them here also means no name\n     * beyond this method's grammar can ever reach a resolver from a request.\n     *\n     * <p>Interface scope ids ({@code fe80::1%9}) never reach here: total += 2;\n                continue;\n            }\n            if (group.isEmpty() || group.length() > 4) {\n                return -1;\n            }\n            for (int c = 0; c < group.length(); c++) {\n                char digit = group.charAt(c);\n                boolean hex = (digit >= '0' && digit <= '9')\n                        || (digit >= 'a' && digit <= 'f')\n is refused here\n     * and degrades to the shared bucket instead.\n     */\n    private static boolean isIpv6Literal(String text) {\n        int compress = text.indexOf(\"::\");\n        if (compress 1) >= 0) {\n            return false;\n        }\n        int head = ipv6Groups(text.substring(0, compress), false);\n        int tail = ipv6Groups(text.substring(compress + 2), true);\n        //
